questions.question: Why keep separate train, validation, and test splits?
options: To evaluate on unseen data
To make each split use a different programming language
To guarantee that every example fits in GPU memory
To avoid recording the dataset version
questions.explanation: Training updates parameters, validation guides choices, and the held-out test set estimates generalization. Reusing test examples for tuning makes its score optimistic.

questions.question: When is streaming=True useful while loading a very large dataset?
options: When the dataset must be converted into a video stream
Fetch rows on demand
When every row must be downloaded before the first example is read
When a stream should silently replace the validation split
questions.explanation: Streaming creates an iterable view that reads examples as needed, reducing local storage and memory pressure. It does not change the meaning of the split.

questions.question: Which format is the natural choice for fast typed column reads from a tabular dataset?
options: CSV, because every reader preserves its inferred types exactly
A plain-text log, because it has schema metadata by default
Columnar, compressed storage
A shell history file, because it supports random row access
questions.explanation: Parquet's columnar layout and schema support make selective reads and compression efficient. CSV remains useful for simple interchange but needs parsing and type handling.

questions.question: What should a reproducible dataset split record besides the three counts?
options: Only the name of the editor used to create the split
The GPU temperature at the time of export
A screenshot with no dataset identifier
The seed, source, split rule, and filters
questions.explanation: Counts alone cannot recreate membership. The seed, source revision, and transformation rules let another run produce and audit the same partitions.

questions.question: A model's test score is suspiciously high after you generated train and test files. What should you inspect first?
options: Check for duplicates and train/test leakage
The color of the dataset directory in the editor
Whether the README uses short paragraphs
The number of CPU threads used by the terminal
questions.explanation: Leakage and duplicates let the model see test information during training, producing an inflated score. Comparing identities and split construction tests that hypothesis directly.

questions.question: What belongs in a compact data card for a phase artifact?
options: Only the final accuracy, with no record of the examples
Schema, counts, seed, source, format, and cache
A copy of every raw file embedded in the source repository
The dataset URL without its revision or preprocessing description
questions.explanation: These fields describe what was loaded and how it became the training inputs. They make the artifact inspectable without putting large data files into Git.
